title: The Cost

canonical_node.axiom: Finitude is the structural condition under which good things can exist; cost is the price of finitude and is distinct from evil, which is the refusal of orientation.
definitions: Structural entropy: the neutral cost of finitude (e.g., fire burns, stars die, cells age).
Moral entropy: the directional fracture of will (e.g., cruelty, deception, murder).
Cost: the price of finitude, structural and not evil.
Evil: the refusal of orientation, directional and not structural.
derivation: A child touching a hot stove learns that fire burns; the burn is the price of heat, not evil.
Removing the burn would remove fire, and thus remove warmth, cooking, metallurgy, stars - removing the possibility of a world that does anything.
Therefore, finitude is not evil but the condition for good things to exist.
Genesis 1:31 says the world is 'very good' - not 'perfectly painless' - so structural costs are part of the design.
Structural entropy (physical decay) is distinct from moral entropy (willful refusal).
The shadow (possibility of refusal) existed before creation as bounded darkness, but was not entered until the Fall.
The Fall was a relational breach (removal of grace-maintenance), not a change in physics.
Grace re-orients the field (G > 0) without changing physics; the Cross is a field-repair event, the Resurrection verifies the repair.
canonical_node.action: The system must distinguish structural entropy from moral entropy in all analyses, treating cost as inherent to finitude and not as evil, and treat the Fall as a relational breach rather than a physical change.
boundary: Does not claim that structural entropy is evil or that God authored evil.
Does not excuse moral entropy as natural.
Does not assert empirical access to pre-Fall vs. post-Fall physics.
Does not derive the full 10-Law entropy or eschatological resolution.
test: Check that any statement about suffering or entropy clearly separates structural from moral causes.
Verify that the Fall is described as a relational breach, not a physics change.
Confirm that 'very good' is interpreted as including finitude's cost, not its absence.

dg1_dependencies: Sheet 2 (The Shadow) - orientation and shadow concept
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a framework to distinguish structural cost from moral evil, enabling theodicy without attributing evil to God or excusing cruelty.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the coherence of creation as 'very good' while acknowledging real suffering and cost.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this distinction, theodicy collapses: either God authors evil or cruelty is excused.
dg5_translation_registers: Physical: entropy as neutral drift vs. willful refusal

overstatement_risks: Claiming the distinction between structural and moral entropy is proven rather than asserted.
Treating the Tree of Life as grace-maintenance as derived rather than interpretive.
Implying empirical knowledge of pre-Fall conditions.
kill_conditions: If structural entropy is shown to be evil, the framework collapses.
If moral entropy is shown to be natural, the framework collapses.
If the Fall is shown to be a physics change, the framework collapses.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the distinction between structural and moral entropy in the Master Equation, and ground the Tree of Life claim theologically.

plain_summary: This document establishes that the world's suffering is not evil but the structural cost of finitude, distinct from moral evil which is the refusal of orientation. It argues that the Fall was a relational breach, not a physics change, and that grace re-orients without removing cost. The framework is coherent but not formally proven.
